q: Had I known about the storm, I ___ the trip.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had I + past participle, would have + past participle. Example: Had I seen you, I'd have waved.

notes.would cancel: Would cancel is about now; the storm was in the past.
notes.had cancelled: Had cancelled can't be the result part.
notes.will have cancelled: Will have isn't used in conditionals about the past.

q: The bridge is thought ___ over 500 years ago.
explain: Passive reporting about the past: is thought to have been + past participle. Example: He is said to have been a king.

notes.to be built: To be built is about now or the future, not 500 years ago.
notes.that it was built: 'That it was built' needs 'It is thought that...'.

q: I'd rather you ___ tell anyone.
explain: Would rather + another person + past simple. Example: I'd rather you stayed.

notes.don't: Don't is present; this structure needs the past.

q: She denied ___ the crystal.
explain: Deny + -ing. Example: He denied breaking the vase.

notes.take: The plain verb can't follow deny.

q: By next summer, they ___ the new castle.
explain: Future perfect: will have + past participle = done before a future time. Example: By 6 pm I'll have finished.

notes.are finishing: Are finishing doesn't fit 'by next summer'.

q: It's high time we ___ home.
explain: It's high time + past simple. Example: It's high time you went to bed.

notes.go: Present go isn't used after 'high time'.

q: The swans, ___ feathers shimmered, glided past.
explain: Whose shows possession. Example: the girl whose bike was stolen.

notes.that: That can't follow a comma or show possession.

q: He must ___ the wrong path; he's still not here.
explain: Must have + past participle = a strong guess about the past. Example: She must have forgotten.

notes.take: Must take is about the present or future.

q: I'm not used to ___ so much attention.
explain: Be used to + -ing. Example: I'm used to living alone.

notes.receive: Plain verb can't follow 'used to' meaning familiar.

q: She'd have won the race if she ___ fallen.
explain: Third conditional: if + had (not) + past participle. Example: If he hadn't slept in, he'd have caught the bus.

notes.wouldn't have: Would never goes in the if-part.

q: ___ by the long journey, the knight fell asleep.
explain: A past participle clause can give the reason: Exhausted = because he was exhausted. Example: Tired by the walk, we sat down.

notes.Exhausting: Exhausting describes what tires you, not the knight.
notes.Having exhaust: Having exhaust is not a correct form.
notes.Exhaust: Exhaust is a plain verb or a noun.

q: You ___ have brought a gift, but it's very kind of you.
explain: Needn't have + past participle = you did it, but it wasn't necessary. Example: You needn't have waited.

notes.mustn't: Mustn't have isn't used for the past.
notes.shouldn't: Shouldn't have = it was wrong, which is unkind here.

q: She's one of the few people ___ can solve the riddle.
explain: Who for people as the subject. Example: the man who lives next door.

notes.whom: Whom is an object; here it's the subject.

q: I regret ___ you that the boat has sunk.
explain: Regret to tell/inform = sorry to give bad news now. Example: We regret to inform you...

notes.telling: Regret telling = sorry you told someone in the past.

q: The more you practise, ___ you become.
explain: The + comparative, the + comparative. Example: The sooner, the better.

notes.the best: Best is a superlative, not a comparative.
notes.more better: More better is a double comparative.

q: Not until the lake froze ___ how cold it was.
explain: After 'Not until...' at the start, invert: did + subject + verb. Example: Not until midnight did she arrive.

notes.we realised: Normal word order isn't allowed after 'Not until'.
notes.we did realise: We did realise has the wrong order.

q: Whatever happens, we ___ to the plan.
explain: Whatever + present, will + verb for the future. Example: Whatever you say, I'll go.

q: If she hadn't missed the ferry, she ___ here by now.
explain: Mixed conditional: past cause, present result (would be). Example: If I'd eaten breakfast, I wouldn't be hungry now.

notes.would have been: Would have been is a past result, but 'by now' is present.
notes.had been: Had been isn't a result form.

q: The results ___ until next week.
explain: Future passive: won't be + past participle. Example: The winner will be announced tomorrow.

notes.won't announce: Won't announce is active: results can't announce.

q: I wish you ___ interrupting me!
explain: Wish + would = we want someone to change an annoying habit. Example: I wish he would stop shouting.

notes.stopped: Stopped is for situations, not annoying behaviour.
notes.had stopped: Had stopped is about the past.

q: He's believed ___ abroad last year.
explain: Is believed to have + past participle for the past. Example: She's thought to have left.

notes.to move: To move is present or future.
notes.to be moved: To be moved is passive: someone moved him.

q: ___ the map more carefully, we wouldn't have got lost.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had we + past participle. Example: Had I known, I'd have helped.

notes.If we read: If we read needs 'had': If we had read.
notes.Were we reading: Were we reading is second conditional style.
notes.Should we read: Should we read is for the future.

q: She insisted ___ for the meal.
explain: Insist on + -ing. Example: He insisted on helping.

q: By the time you get this letter, I ___ the mountains.
explain: Future perfect for an action finished before a future moment. Example: By Friday I'll have read it.

q: They had the old tower ___ last spring.
explain: Have something + past participle = someone else does it for you. Example: I had my hair cut.

notes.to restore: To restore doesn't follow 'had the tower'.

q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
explain: After 'Not only' at the start, invert: was he. Example: Not only is she kind, but she's also funny.

notes.he was: He was is normal order; inversion is needed.
notes.he is: He is is present and normal order.

q: You needn't ___ me a lift; I could have walked.
explain: Needn't have + past participle = done, but not necessary. Example: You needn't have cooked.

q: There's no point ___ about it now.
explain: There's no point + -ing. Example: There's no point crying.

notes.worried: Worried is an adjective or past.

q: The guide, ___ we'd met the day before, showed us a shortcut.
explain: Whom = a person as the object (we met him). Example: the friend whom I visited.

q: Supposing you ___ the lottery, what would you do?
explain: Supposing works like 'if' in the second conditional: past simple. Example: Supposing it snowed, would we go?

notes.win: Win is first conditional, but 'would' needs the past.
notes.had won: Had won is for the past (third conditional).

q: It's no use ___ to him; he never listens.
explain: It's no use + -ing. Example: It's no use crying.

q: If we ___ the map, we wouldn't have got lost in the maze.
explain: Third conditional (imaginary past): If + had + past participle, would have + past participle. Example: If I had known, I would have come.

notes.checked: Checked is second conditional (present/future), but this is about the past.
notes.would check: Would never goes in the if-clause.
notes.have checked: Have checked is present perfect, not the past perfect we need.

q: If the robot ___ properly, we would have won the science fair.
explain: Third conditional: If + past perfect for an imaginary past. Example: If it had rained, we'd have stayed in.

notes.worked: Worked makes it a present/future situation.
notes.would work: Would doesn't go in the if-clause.

q: She would have caught the bus if she ___ up earlier.
explain: Third conditional: the if-clause uses had + past participle. Example: if she had left earlier…

q: If I hadn't stayed up gaming, I ___ so tired now.
explain: Mixed conditional: past cause (had + p.p.) → present result (would + verb). Example: If I'd eaten breakfast, I wouldn't be hungry now.

notes.wouldn't have been: Wouldn't have been talks about the past, but 'now' shows the present.
notes.won't be: Won't is for real future possibilities.
notes.hadn't been: Hadn't been belongs in the if-clause, not the result.

q: If she were braver, she ___ for the lead role last week.
explain: Mixed conditional: present state (were) → past result (would have + p.p.). Example: If I were taller, I'd have joined the team last year.

notes.would audition: Would audition is present/future, but 'last week' is past.
notes.had auditioned: Had auditioned belongs in an if-clause.
notes.auditioned: Auditioned is a real past fact, not imaginary.

q: ___ you need any help with the project, just send me a message.
explain: Should at the start = 'if' for a possible future need (formal). Example: Should you have questions, ask me.

notes.Had: Had + you is for imaginary past: Had you known…
notes.Were: Were you is followed by to-infinitive or an adjective, not need.

q: ___ I known the test was today, I'd have revised.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had + subject + p.p. = If + had. Example: Had we left earlier, we'd have caught it.

notes.If: If would need had too: If I had known.
notes.Were: Were I is for present imaginary situations.
notes.Should: Should is for possible future events.

q: I'll lend you my scooter ___ you're careful with it.
explain: As long as = only if. Example: You can play as long as you finish your homework.

notes.unless: Unless means if not, the opposite meaning.
notes.in case: In case = because something might happen.
notes.even if: Even if = whether or not, which doesn't make it a condition.

q: ___ it rains, the sports day will go ahead.
explain: Even if = whatever happens, the result stays the same. Example: Even if I'm tired, I'll finish.

notes.Unless: Unless would mean it only goes ahead if it doesn't rain.
notes.Provided: Provided means only if it rains, which is odd.
notes.As long as: As long as makes rain a requirement.

q: But for your help, I ___ the puzzle.
explain: But for + noun = if it hadn't been for. Example: But for the map, we'd have got lost.

notes.didn't finish: Didn't finish is a real fact, not imaginary.
notes.won't finish: Won't is for real future events.
notes.hadn't finished: Hadn't finished needs to be in an if-clause.

q: I wish I ___ to the concert last night. Everyone says it was amazing.
explain: Wish + past perfect = regret about the past. Example: I wish I had studied more.

notes.went: Went after wish is for the present.
notes.would go: Would after wish is for annoying habits or wanting change.
notes.have gone: Have gone is present perfect; wish needs the past perfect.

q: I wish I ___ play the guitar. It looks so fun.
explain: Wish + could = an ability you'd like to have now. Example: I wish I could fly.

notes.am able: Am able needs to and isn't used after wish.

q: I wish my little brother ___ touching my things!
explain: Wish + would = annoyance at someone's behaviour. Example: I wish you would listen.

notes.stopped to: Stopped to means stopped in order to.

q: If only we ___ more time to finish the castle model!
explain: If only + past = a wish about now. Example: If only it were Saturday!

notes.have: Have is present; after if only we step back to the past.
notes.would have: Would have is for past results.

q: It's time you ___ to bed. It's nearly eleven!
explain: It's (high) time + past simple = you should do it now. Example: It's time we left.

notes.go: Go isn't used after it's time + subject.
notes.going: Going isn't a full verb here.

q: I'd rather you ___ my diary. It's private.
explain: I'd rather + person + past simple = what I want someone else to do. Example: I'd rather you stayed.

notes.don't read: Don't read is present, but this pattern needs the past.

q: The lights are off. They ___ gone to bed already.
explain: Must have + p.p. = I'm sure it happened. Example: She must have left.

notes.can't have: Can't have means I'm sure it didn't happen.
notes.should: Should is advice, and needs 'have gone' anyway.

q: He ___ seen the ghost. Ghosts aren't real!
explain: Can't have + p.p. = I'm sure it didn't happen. Example: She can't have eaten it all!

notes.mustn't have: Mustn't isn't used for deduction in British English.
notes.must have: Must have means you're sure it did happen.

q: I'm not sure where my phone is. I ___ left it on the bus.
explain: Might/may/could have + p.p. = perhaps it happened. Example: He might have forgotten.

notes.must: Must left is missing have, and must is too sure.
notes.should have: Should have means it was the right thing to do.
notes.can have: Can have isn't used for past possibility.

q: You ___ told me about the test! I didn't revise at all.
explain: Should have + p.p. = criticism of a past action. Example: You should have asked.

notes.must have: Must have is deduction, not criticism.
notes.had to: Had to told isn't a form.

q: We ___ taken umbrellas. It didn't rain after all.
explain: Needn't have + p.p. = we did it, but it wasn't necessary. Example: I needn't have worried.

notes.mustn't have: Mustn't have isn't a past modal for necessity.
notes.didn't need: Didn't need taken is wrong: didn't need to take.

q: She ___ be at home. Her bike's outside.
explain: Must = I'm sure (present deduction). Example: You must be tired after the race.

notes.can't: Can't means you're sure she isn't.
notes.might not: Might not doesn't match the clue of the bike.
notes.needn't: Needn't is about necessity, not deduction.

q: The test ___ be that hard; everyone finished early.
explain: Can't = I'm sure it isn't true. Example: That can't be right.

notes.mustn't: Mustn't is a rule, not a deduction.
notes.must: Must would mean you're sure it was hard.

q: The new skate park ___ at the moment.
explain: Present continuous passive: is/are being + p.p. Example: The road is being repaired.

notes.is building: Is building makes the park the builder.

q: The winners ___ by the time we arrived.
explain: Past perfect passive: had been + p.p. Example: The cake had been eaten.

notes.had already chosen: Had chosen is active: the winners chose something.
notes.have already been chosen: Have been is present perfect, but 'arrived' is past.

q: The dinosaur bones are said ___ 70 million years old.
explain: Be said/thought/believed + to-infinitive. Example: He is said to be very kind.

notes.to have: To have would need a past participle.

q: The pyramids are thought ___ by thousands of workers.
explain: Passive report about the past: to have been + p.p. Example: The castle is believed to have been built in 1200.

notes.to be built: To be built is about now or the future.
notes.to have built: To have built is active: the pyramids built something.
notes.being built: Being built doesn't follow are thought.

q: It ___ that the comet will be visible on Friday.
explain: It + is + reporting verb (passive) + that. Example: It is believed that he left.

notes.expects: Expects is active and needs a subject who expects.

q: I'm having my bedroom ___ next week.
explain: Have something done = someone else does it for you. Example: I had my hair cut.

notes.paint: Paint is the base form; we need the past participle.
notes.to paint: To paint doesn't follow have + object here.
notes.painting: Painting would mean the room is doing the painting.

q: She got her phone screen ___ after she dropped it.
explain: Get something done = arrange for someone to do it. Example: We got the car washed.

notes.repairing: Repairing doesn't fit get + object here.
notes.to repair: To repair doesn't fit this pattern.

q: The match ___ because of the storm.
explain: Modal passive: modal + be + p.p. Example: The homework must be finished.

notes.had to cancel: Had to cancel is active: the match cancelled something.
notes.must cancel: Must cancel is active and present.

q: The coach ___ us to warm up properly.
explain: Remind/tell/ask + person + to-infinitive. Example: She reminded me to bring my kit.

notes.said: Say doesn't take a person + to: said to us that…
notes.suggested: Suggest isn't followed by person + to.
notes.explained: Explain isn't followed by person + to.

q: Ella suggested ___ a film instead.
explain: Suggest + -ing (or that + subject + verb). Example: He suggested going home.

notes.us to watch: Suggest isn't followed by person + to.
notes.watch: Watch needs -ing or that we watch.

q: He apologised ___ late for rehearsal.
explain: Apologise for + -ing. Example: She apologised for shouting.

notes.that being: That being isn't a correct pattern.

q: My friend admitted ___ the last cookie.
explain: Admit + -ing (or admit to + -ing). Example: He admitted breaking the vase.

notes.to eating it: The it repeats the object: the last cookie.

q: She asked me where ___.
explain: Reported questions use statement word order and backshift. Example: He asked what time it was.

notes.was the library: Was the library is question order.
notes.is the library: Is the library is question order and present.

q: Our teacher warned us ___ the electric fence.
explain: Warn + person + not to + verb. Example: She warned me not to be late.

notes.to not touching: To not touching mixes two forms.

q: He accused his brother ___ his headphones.
explain: Accuse someone of + -ing. Example: They accused him of cheating.

notes.for breaking: Accuse goes with of, not for.
notes.about breaking: Accuse goes with of, not about.

q: I'll never forget ___ the northern lights for the first time.
explain: Forget + -ing = a memory of the past. Example: I'll never forget meeting her.

notes.to see: Forget to see = not remember to do it.
notes.to have seen: To have seen doesn't follow forget here.

q: Don't forget ___ the hamster before you leave.
explain: Forget + to-infinitive = not remember to do a task. Example: Don't forget to lock the door.

notes.feeding: Forget feeding is about a past memory.

q: He tried ___ the lid, but it was stuck.
explain: Try + to = make an effort (it's difficult). Example: I tried to lift it.

notes.opening: Try + -ing = do it as an experiment to see if it helps.
notes.to opening: To opening isn't a form here.

q: If the plant looks sad, try ___ it some water.
explain: Try + -ing = do something as an experiment. Example: Try restarting the computer.

notes.to give: Try to give = make an effort, but giving water isn't difficult.
notes.to giving: To giving isn't a form here.

q: After the maths lesson, we went on ___ the science project.
explain: Go on + to = move on to something new. Example: She went on to become a pilot.

notes.doing: Go on doing = continue the same thing.
notes.to doing: To doing isn't a form here.

q: I regret ___ so rude to my friend yesterday.
explain: Regret + -ing = be sorry about the past. Example: I regret saying that.

notes.to be: Regret to = formal: I'm sorry to tell you.

q: She's used to ___ up early for swim training.
explain: Be used to + -ing = be familiar with. Example: I'm used to living here.

notes.get: After be used to we need -ing.
notes.to get: Used to get (no be) is a past habit.

q: I'd prefer ___ at home tonight.
explain: Would prefer + to-infinitive. Example: I'd prefer to walk.

notes.staying: Prefer -ing is for general likes, not 'would prefer'.

q: The joke was so funny that I couldn't stop ___.
explain: Stop + -ing = finish doing. Example: Stop talking!

notes.to laugh: Stop to laugh = stop in order to laugh.

q: The planet, ___ is the largest in our solar system, has a giant storm.
explain: Non-defining relative clauses (with commas) use which, not that. Example: My bike, which is red, is new.

notes.that: That can't be used after a comma.
notes.what: What can't be a relative pronoun here.

q: The scientist ___ invention we tested is coming to our school.
explain: Whose = belonging to. Example: The girl whose dog barks.

q: This is the spot ___ we found the fossil.
explain: Where = in/at which (place). Example: The town where I grew up.

notes.which: Which would need a preposition: in which.
notes.that: That would need 'at' at the end.

q: The friend ___ I told my secret kept it safe.
explain: Preposition + whom (formal). Example: The person to whom I spoke.

notes.whom: Tell someone something needs to: told it to whom.
notes.to who: After a preposition we use whom, not who.

q: He failed the test, ___ surprised everyone.
explain: Which can refer to a whole clause. Example: She laughed, which annoyed him.

notes.what: What can't refer back to a clause.

q: I have three cousins, all of ___ live in Canada.
explain: Quantifier + of + whom/which. Example: two dogs, both of which bark.

notes.them: Them would make two sentences joined by a comma.

q: ___ the door, she saw a huge cake on the table.
explain: Present participle clause: two actions by the same person, one after the other. Example: Walking home, I saw a fox.

notes.Opened: Opened is passive: the door opened her.
notes.Having open: Having open is missing -ed: having opened.

q: ___ his homework, Leo went out to play.
explain: Having + p.p. = one action completed before another. Example: Having eaten, we left.

q: ___ in 1903, the first plane flew for only 12 seconds.
explain: Past participle clause = passive meaning. Example: Made of glass, the vase broke.

notes.Building: Building would mean the plane was building something.

q: The boy ___ next to me is my cousin.
explain: Reduced relative clause: noun + -ing = who is doing. Example: The girl wearing red.

notes.sat down: Sat down would need 'who': who sat down.

q: Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.
explain: Negative adverb first → inversion. Example: Never have I been so tired.

notes.I have seen: After never we invert: have I.
notes.I saw: Past simple would need did I see.
notes.seen I have: Seen I have is wrong word order.

q: Not only ___ the race, but she also broke the record.
explain: Not only + inversion, but also… Example: Not only is it fast, but it's also cheap.

notes.she did win: She did win is normal order.

q: No sooner had we sat down ___ the fire alarm went off.
explain: No sooner … than. Example: No sooner had I left than it rained.

notes.then: Then isn't used in this pattern.

q: Hardly ___ the lights gone out when the ghost story began.
explain: Hardly + had + subject + p.p. + when. Example: Hardly had I arrived when it started.

notes.have: Have is present perfect; the story is in the past.
notes.were: Were doesn't go with gone here.

q: This time next week, we ___ on the beach in Bali!
explain: Future continuous: an action in progress at a future time. Example: At 8, I'll be eating.

notes.will lie: Will lie is one action, not in progress.
notes.are lying: Are lying would be a fixed plan, but we need in-progress.
notes.will have lain: Will have lain = finished by then.

q: By the end of term, I ___ ten books for the reading challenge.
explain: Future perfect: done before a future time. Example: By 6, I'll have finished.

notes.will read: Will read doesn't show completion by a time.
notes.will be reading: Will be reading is in progress, not completed.

q: The train ___ at 7:15 tomorrow, so don't be late.
explain: Present simple for timetables. Example: The film starts at 8.

notes.will be leaving: Will be leaving is possible but less natural for a timetable.
notes.is going to leave: Going to is for plans or predictions, not timetables.

q: Look at those clouds! It ___ pour any minute.
explain: Be about to = very soon. Example: The film is about to start.

notes.will be: Will be pour isn't a form.
notes.is on: Is on isn't a future form.

q: We ___ to visit the space museum, but it was closed.
explain: Was/were going to = a past plan that didn't happen. Example: I was going to call, but I forgot.

notes.are going: Are going is a present plan, but it was closed.

q: ___ the fact that it was raining, we played outside.
explain: Despite + noun/-ing. Example: Despite the cold, we swam.

notes.Although: Although needs a clause: although it was raining.
notes.Even though: Even though needs a subject + verb: even though it was raining.

q: He's ___ talented that he could play for the national team.
explain: So + adjective + that. Example: It was so cold that we stayed in.

notes.such: Such needs a noun: such a talented player.
notes.too: Too + adjective means more than enough.

q: It was ___ an exciting match that nobody left early.
explain: Such + (a/an) + adjective + noun + that. Example: She's such a good friend.

notes.so: So doesn't go before a/an + noun.
notes.too: Too doesn't fit with a noun here.

q: There's ___ time left, so hurry up!
explain: Little + uncountable (not much). Example: There's little milk.

notes.a few: A few is for countable nouns.

q: ___ of my friends likes horror films; they all hate them.
explain: None of + plural group = not one. Example: None of the cakes are left.

notes.Neither: Neither is only for two people.
notes.No one: No one can't be followed by of.
notes.Nothing: Nothing is for things, not friends.

q: You can borrow ___ book. I like them both.
explain: Either + singular noun = one or the other of two. Example: Either day is fine.

notes.neither: Neither would mean you can't borrow one.
notes.any of: Any of needs the: any of the books.

q: I'll finish the poster ___ Friday at the latest.
explain: By + time = no later than. Example: Hand it in by Monday.

notes.until: Until means continuing up to then.
notes.since: Since is for a starting point.
notes.for: For is for a period of time.

q: We waited ___ midnight to see the meteor shower.
explain: Until = continuing up to a time. Example: I'll wait until six.

notes.by: By = no later than, not continuing.
notes.since: Since is for a starting point in the past.
notes.during: During needs a period: during the night.

q: We've lived here ___ I was six.
explain: Since + a point in time with present perfect. Example: since 2020.

notes.for: For is for a length of time.
notes.ago: Ago follows a time: two years ago.

q: The test was hard. ___, most of us passed.
explain: Nevertheless = however, at the start of a new sentence. Example: It rained. Nevertheless, we went.

notes.Despite: Despite needs a noun after it.
notes.Although: Although joins two clauses in one sentence.
notes.Because: Because gives a reason, not contrast.

q: I'll take some snacks ___ we get hungry on the hike.
explain: In case = as a precaution because it might happen. Example: Take a coat in case it's cold.

notes.so that: So that shows purpose, and needs a different verb.
notes.otherwise: Otherwise means if not, and needs a comma clause.

q: She practised every day ___ win the competition.
explain: So as to / in order to + verb = purpose. Example: I left early so as to catch the bus.

notes.so that: So that needs a subject: so that she could win.
notes.in case: In case is a precaution, not a purpose.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: If I had known, I would have helped you.
explain: Third conditional: If + had + pp, would have + pp.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: By the time we arrived, the show had started.
explain: Past perfect for the earlier action.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: She suggested that we take a different path.
explain: suggest that + plain verb.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Not only is he funny, but he is also kind.
explain: Not only + inversion.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: The bridge is being repaired at the moment.
explain: Present continuous passive: is being + pp.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb: The news is…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Despite has no 'of' (in spite of does).

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Everyone is singular: Everyone was…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: be used to + -ing.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Advice: If I were you.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: The number (singular) has grown.
